extracted.intended_audience: school administrators, Title IX coordinators, legal counsel, and other recipients of federal education funding
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards and interpretive guidance from the Department of Education's Title IX final rule preamble concerning what constitutes sex discrimination in education programs and activities, including specific protected bases, harm thresholds, privacy, and training obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination based on sexual orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations prohibit discrimination on the basis of sexual orientation under §106.10. A recipient's intentional separation or different treatment of students based on their sexual orientation generally would constitute sex discrimination under the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department recognizes sexual orientation as distinct from sex but explains that when regulations permit separation on the basis of 'sex,' they do not permit separation on the basis of sexual orientation or other bases in §106.10 (e.g., pregnancy or sex stereotypes). Cf. Bostock, 590 U.S. at 659-62.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination based on sex characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.10 prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex characteristics, including intersex traits; 'sex characteristics' are intended to refer to physiological sex-based characteristics (anatomy, hormones, chromosomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department: (1) rejects the need for a medical diagnosis to substantiate such discrimination; (2) states sex-characteristics discrimination may be rooted in perceived differences between an individual's characteristics and those considered typical for their sex assigned at birth; (3) gives examples (inappropriate disclosure of medical information, denial of access to sex-separate facilities consistent with gender identity) but declines to make definitive examples because analysis is fact-specific; and (4) notes it uses the term 'intersex' for accessibility while recognizing the spectrum of conditions (citing Consortium guidelines). Changes: None.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination based on sex stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sex stereotyping—'fixed or generalized expectations regarding a person's aptitudes, behavior, self-presentation, or other attributes based on sex'—can constitute sex discrimination when it operates to exclude, deny benefits to, or otherwise subject a person to discrimination under a recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department applies Price Waterhouse reasoning and court precedent (e.g., Whitaker, Pederson) to hold sex stereotyping can be a form of sex discrimination under Title IX. Not all conduct labeled 'sex stereotyping' violates Title IX; to be actionable it must, on the basis of sex, exclude a person from participation, deny benefits, or otherwise discriminate. Permissible sex separation remains allowed only if carried out without imposing more than de minimis harm (see §106.31(a)(2)). Changes: None.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on discrimination based on pregnancy or related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.10 makes clear Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination includes discrimination on the basis of pregnancy or related conditions across a recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains pregnancy-related discrimination has long been prohibited but that §106.10 provides needed clarity. The rule covers harassment based on pregnancy, and related harassment that impedes access to education. The Department declines to add 'current, potential, or past' to §106.10 because §§106.21(c), 106.40(b)(1), and 106.57(b) already address those modifiers; it also relies on the separate definitional text in §106.2. Where a menstruation-related condition meets the §106.2 definition, reasonable modifications under §106.40(b)(3)(ii) may apply. Changes: None.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of menstruation and related conditions as sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrimination based on menstruation, perimenopause, menopause, or related conditions is sex discrimination because it can overlap with pregnancy or related conditions, sex stereotypes, or sex characteristics under §106.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department: (1) explains biological basis (menstruation triggered by hormones, etc.); (2) lists associated medical conditions (PMS, migraines, heavy bleeding) as potentially implicated; (3) affirms harassment, bathroom restrictions, exposure of menstruation, and related discipline can be barriers requiring recipient action under §106.44(a) and (f)(1); (4) declines to add explicit regulatory text requiring menstrual products or mandatory reasonable modifications but will study the issue further; (5) notes disability law (Section 504/ADA) may separately entitle remedies; (6) gives examples of reasonable accommodations that may be required under existing nondiscrimination protections. Changes: None.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy of menstruation-related and other personally identifiable records
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must not disclose personally identifiable information obtained in the course of complying with these regulations, with limited exceptions (revised §106.44(j)), and should collect no more information than necessary per §106.8(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department agrees privacy concerns warrant clarification: Title IX Coordinators may not share an individual's menstruation-related information with law enforcement or keep it in a disclosable student record except as permitted. The Department revised §106.44(j) to clarify the prohibition on disclosure of personally identifiable information. The Department will offer technical assistance on implementation. Changes: Revised §106.44(j) to clarify nondisclosure of personally identifiable information except limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training obligations for employees (scope and flexibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.8(d)(1), all employees must be trained on the recipient's obligation to address sex discrimination and the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to mandate specific training content beyond this general requirement to allow recipient flexibility. Because menstruation and related conditions fall within §106.10, recipients may benefit from including them in employee and Title IX Coordinator trainings; the Department may provide future guidance and technical assistance, but does not require menstrual education for students (it does not control curricula). Changes: None.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis harm standard for permissible sex separation (§106.31(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissible sex separation under §106.31(a)(2) must be carried out in a manner that does not impose more than de minimis harm on affected students; harm must be genuine and objectively non-trivial, assessed from the perspective of a reasonable person in the individual's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains the de minimis harm standard is grounded in discrimination case law (injury/harm element) and judicial precedent (Oncale, Burlington N. & Santa Fe Ry. Co., Bostock). The standard distinguishes innocuous sex-based differences from actionable discrimination and recognizes stigmatic injuries may suffice. The Department rejects arguments that the standard is vague or inconsistent with Title IX; it clarifies the inquiry is objective and judicially administrable. Changes: None.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to address barriers, prevent recurrence, and remedy effects (§106.44)
rubrics_metrics.description: When discrimination (including menstruation- or pregnancy-related discrimination) becomes a barrier to participation, schools have an obligation to address such barriers, prevent their recurrence, and remedy their effects, per §106.44(a) and (f)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cites §106.44 as the mechanism requiring recipients to act where discrimination impedes access. Examples include addressing menstruation-related harassment, unreasonable bathroom access limits, or conduct that publicly exposes a student's menstruation. Records of complaints and steps taken should be maintained consistent with §106.8(f) but without unnecessary collection of sensitive information. Changes: The Department revised §106.44(j) (privacy) and will provide technical assistance to promote compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Department authority and consistency with statutory/case law
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department characterizes §§106.10 and 106.31(a)(2) as consistent with Title IX's statutory objectives and Federal court decisions, and rejects application of the major questions doctrine to invalidate these regulatory choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department asserts express statutory authority (20 U.S.C. 1682) to issue regulations 'consistent with achievement of the objectives of the statute,' points to prior regulatory and case-law practice, and argues the rules do not effect the kind of unprecedented, transformative action implicated in West Virginia v. EPA. It also notes the final regulations are grounded in court interpretations (e.g., Bostock) and Department expertise. This is used to justify the interpretation and application of the substantive protections above. Changes: None.
